taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce angusta is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Dry-country spurge with narrow leaves and a more upright to spreading habit than the tiny mat-forming sandmats.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew accepts Euphorbia angusta, native from western Texas to Coahuila.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae/Euphorbia: milky latex and highly reduced flowers grouped into a cyathium; in sandmat spurges, opposite leaves, stem habit, hairiness, and capsule traits are especially useful.
best_field_traits: narrow linear to narrowly oblong leaves
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Within this batch, E. angusta is the narrow-leaved dry-country species. It is less mat-forming than E. serpens or E. prostrata and much less hairy than E. villifera.
